evidence: Wikipedia's article on the album 'Tom Tom Club': recorded at Compass Point Studios in Nassau between November 1980 and April 1981, and released by Island Records in the UK (Sire in the US). Compass Point was Chris Blackwell's studio, and Island's house band there is already on the map (e-island-slyrobbie). Jamaican session musicians Tyrone Downie and Uziah 'Sticky' Thompson played on the record.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Both came out of Compass Point in 1981. 'Pull Up to the Bumper' is Sly and Robbie's rhythm section under Grace Jones: heavy, slow, reggae-funk. 'Genius of Love' is lighter and bouncier, but listen for the same loose, rolling bass and the same room. Island's Bahamas studio was producing a sound, and two very different acts shared it.

explanation: Tom Tom Club made their first album at Compass Point, Island Records' studio in the Bahamas, and Island released it in Britain. Island owned the room and released the record, and the studio's players and sound are part of why a Talking Heads side project came out sounding like a Caribbean dance record.
